reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g1_mg_q1_0), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The items directly fulfill the target competency of identifying simple 2D shapes (triangles, rectangles, and squares). Triangles are identified through real-world context ("A party hat is shaped with 3 straight edges. What 2D shape is it?") and direct shape prompts ("A small flat shape with 3 straight edges is shown. What shape is it?"). Rectangles are identified via properties ("A classroom chalkboard has 4 straight edges and opposite edges are equal. What shape is the chalkboard?"), and squares are evaluated via equal edge descriptions ("A flat floor tile has 4 equal straight edges. What shape is the tile?"). Variations in size ("A large flat shape with 4 equal straight edges is shown. What shape is it?") and orientation ("A small triangular sign is turned upside down. What shape is it?") are explicitly tested.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set comprehensively covers all three specified shapes—triangle, rectangle, and square. It also covers both abstract geometric descriptions (e.g., "A small flat shape with 3 straight edges is shown. What shape is it?") and concrete real-world objects (party hats, chalkboards, floor tiles, signs). Crucially, the sub-attributes of the competency—different sizes ("small", "large") and orientation ("turned upside down" in "A small triangular sign is turned upside down. What shape is it?")—are all adequately represented across the batch.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: All sample items are well within the cognitive capacity and reading abilities of a Grade 1 Quarter 1 student. Sentences are concise, syntactic structures are simple, and vocabulary is accessible ("party hat", "chalkboard", "flat shape", "straight edges", "tile"). The focus remains purely on foundational visual and structural identification of 2D shapes without extraneous computational load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The batch demonstrates healthy variation across both formatters (mcq, read_mcq) and contexts. Scenarios span everyday items ("A classroom chalkboard has 4 straight edges and opposite edges are equal. What shape is the chalkboard?", "A flat floor tile has 4 equal straight edges. What shape is the tile?"), rotated objects ("A small triangular sign is turned upside down. What shape is it?"), and pure geometric representations ("A large flat shape with 4 equal straight edges is shown. What shape is it?").

competency_alignment.rationale: Every single question strictly aligns with MATATAG node mat_g1_mg_q1_0. There is no out-of-scope material (e.g., perimeter/area calculations, 3D solids, complex polygon naming, or formal angle definitions). Questions focus purely on distinguishing 2D shapes by edge counts and equal opposite/all sides, fully matching the curricular mandate.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numeric attributes involved (counting 3 or 4 straight edges) are perfectly scaled for Grade 1 Quarter 1 learners who are working with basic single-digit counts up to 10.
